correctness.rationale: Functional digraphs are precisely labeled sets of cycles of rooted in-trees; recurrence T_h=z exp(T_{h-1}), cycle restriction F_{h,d}, exact-depth subtraction and period Möbius inversion are valid for all n,h,p. The threshold is the maximum tail depth and eventual period the cycle-length lcm. Every monoid has exactly phi(p) generating transformations if depth=0 or1, and exactly one if depth>=2. The finite total correction follows by choosing the cyclic vertex set and arbitrary one-step tails. The exponential bound follows from the positive-coefficient EGF 1/(1-z exp(z)) at z=1/2. Literal brute enumerations at all n<=6 and an independent partition-sum calculation to n=12 agree; no finite test is substituted for the proof.

value.rationale: The paper motivating the question classifies isomorphism types but the exact number of different subsets of the full transformation monoid remains a separate natural invariant. The theorem computes the full bivariate embedded multiplicity by depth and period rather than merely counting attainable types; its integer totals through n=12 are reproducible, and the rarity bound shows almost all transformations uniquely generate their own submonoid. In degree six, 42488 embedded monoids contrast with only 22 abstract types, demonstrating a quantitatively material gap. This is a complete classification and census over all finite degrees, not a one-off lookup or arbitrary restricted slice.
